newsitem.title: CROATIA: Tudjman, Izetbegovic have first meeting since poll.
newsitem.headline: Tudjman, Izetbegovic have first meeting since poll.

text.p: Presidents Franjo Tudjman of Croatia and Alija Izetbegovic of Bosnia met on Friday for the first time since the Bosnian leader emerged victorious from his country's post-war elections earlier this month.

The two men made no comment to reporters after the talks, but Tudjman's office issued a statement saying they had "agreed that they should persist in consistently implementing the Dayton and Washington agreements".

Tudjman and Izetbegovic also agreed "it was necessary to form joint bodies as soon as possible and after the elections in Bosnia-Hercegovina", the statement, a copy of which was faxed to Reuters, added.
They also called for a session of the Joint Council for Cooperation between Croatia and the Moslem-Croat Bosnian Federation to be held as a matter of urgency.

Izetbegovic, a Moslem, won a majority of votes in the September 14 Bosnian poll, defeating Bosnian Serb and Croat candidates, and was effectively re-elected as the chairman of Bosnia's three-man presidency for the next two years.
Izetbegovic's relations with Tudjman have never really mended since a 10-month war between Moslems and Croats in 1993 on the fringe of the main Serb-Moslem conflict in Bosnia.
Western diplomats and the Sarajevo government believe only immense western pressure has kept the Bosnian Croats in a federation with the Moslems instead of breaking away to join Croatia.

In a speech to the United Nations General Assembly earlier in New York, Izetbegovic warned of the prospect of renewed conflict if major powers did not do more to enforce the terms of last year's Dayton peace agreement. His speech drew angry reactions from Bosnian Serbs and Croats.
